message.content: A repair cafe in the church hall, one Saturday a month. People throw away kettles and lamps that need one solder joint.
Two things decide whether this is a nice idea or a real one: who fixes, and what happens when a fix goes wrong.

description: The same seeded board as 'The round is answered', driven. Amending an answer on a board with nothing left open arms the countdown that ends the round without anyone pressing anything — and then one keystroke in the chat holds it open again, which is the promise the automation is allowed to exist on. This is the app-route proof rather than the component one: the trigger reads real server-rendered nodes, and the phase action underneath is reachable from the board a person actually looks at. The conversation is collapsed to its input row because the transcript sits over the card being amended; the draft still in the composer is the reason the round did not go.

interactions.value: A rota of two or three, plus whoever is curious that week.
